semantic_correction.stem: A client has completed active cancer treatment and asks what survivorship follow-up care is intended to address. Which response by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: Monitor for recurrence or new health problems, assess treatment-related late effects, and address physical and emotional needs.
options.B: Schedule follow-up when new symptoms occur because routine post-treatment visits are generally unnecessary.
options.C: Limit survivorship care to recurrence monitoring and manage treatment effects or psychosocial needs outside follow-up care.
options.D: Use the same follow-up schedule for every survivor regardless of cancer type, treatment, health status, or late effects.

semantic_correction.rationale: The National Cancer Institute states that all cancer survivors should receive follow-up care after treatment. Follow-up visits can monitor for cancer recurrence or other health changes, evaluate problems caused by treatment including late effects, and address physical and emotional concerns. NCI also emphasizes that follow-up schedules are individualized according to the type of cancer, treatment received, overall health, and treatment-related problems. Therefore option A best describes survivorship follow-up care.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Describe cancer survivorship follow-up as individualized ongoing care that addresses recurrence surveillance, treatment-related late effects, and physical and psychosocial health needs.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed repeated 'only' distractor cueing, shortened the uniquely long correct answer, and preserved NCI's individualized follow-up model covering recurrence, late effects, and physical/emotional needs.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item accurately tests comprehensive individualized cancer-survivorship follow-up without recurrence-only or symptom-trigger-only limitations.

option_audit.A: Correct. It reflects NCI's comprehensive survivorship follow-up domains.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. NCI recommends ongoing follow-up care rather than symptom-triggered visits alone.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Survivorship follow-up includes treatment-related and psychosocial concerns in addition to recurrence surveillance.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Follow-up timing and content are individualized to cancer type, treatment, overall health, and treatment-related problems.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone includes the major NCI follow-up domains without an unsupported limitation.
cueing_check: All four options are survivorship-follow-up descriptions of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
